Definition: probably of foreign derivation; some imported creature, probably a peacock
BiblicalUsage: tukkîy stands behind the English phrase a peacock. In 1 Kings 10:22, apes, and peacocks, and it appears again in 2 Chronicles 9:21.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that God put tukkîy exactly where it is, and I trust His placing of it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
